content: S3 conditional writes (AWS official): If-None-Match:* on PutObject/CopyObject/CompleteMultipartUpload gives create-if-not-exists — succeeds 200 if no current object with that key, else 412 Precondition Failed; concurrent conditional writes: first to finish wins, rest get 412; concurrent-delete races yield 409 Conflict (If-None-Match) or 404 (If-Match); requires SigV4; If-Match with an ETag gives compare-and-write. ETag is MD5-derived for single-part uploads (not a multihash); for content-addressed data the CID in the key is the real integrity identity, so idempotent retry safety comes from write-once keys with identical bytes, with If-None-Match:* as the create-only guard and 412 mapped to already-exists success semantics. s3d independently implements the same If-None-Match/If-Match behavior — cross-verified across two implementations.
